title: A rapid and simple protocol for the isolation of bacteriophages from coastal organisms
author: Echeverría-Vega, Morales-Vicencio, et al.
materials: To count the bacterial cells in the suspension, the sample was treated with DAPI fluorescent dye (4′,6-diamine-2- phenylindole-dilactate, Merck) [3]. After DAPI staining, three 10 mL serial dilutions (1/10, 1/100 and 1/1000) were performed and 4 % paraformaldehyde was added to each. The solutions were filtered using 0.22 μm pore size polycarbonate membranes (Merck, Millipore), and the filters were allowed to dry for 15 min over absorbent paper. 15 μL of a 2 mg/L DAPI solution, was placed on a slide, covered with the filters and incubated in a dark damp box for 15 min at room temperature. The filters were removed and washed in 96 % ethanol for 10 s and further dried on absorbent paper for one hour at 37 °C in the dark. Dry filters were mounted on a slide with 10 μL of Vecta Shield mounting medium (Vector Labs) and covered with a clean cover glass. Stained cells were observed in a fluorescence microscope with a filter set of ∼359 nm λ excitation and ∼461 nm λ emission, using a 100x lens with a standardized 10 × 10 μm quadrant in the eyepiece as counting grid. A minimum of 500 cells was counted for each sample and the dilution was chosen that allow the required fields to be stated. The total number of cells per sample was estimated by establishing the ratio between counting area and the total effective filtration area of the polycarbonate filter. This value was multiplied by the number of counted cells and the dilution factor and divided by the total filtered volume as showed in the equation:(A*X[cells]*f)(a*1[mL])-1where, A is the filtration area; X is the number of counted cells; f is the dilution factor, and a is the area of the field observed under the microscope.

Benthic filter-feeder mollusks (mytilid mussels) were collected from the coastal zone of Antofagasta, Chile. These were placed in sterile containers and processed on the same day of collection. First, 100 g of soft tissue were extracted from the shells and homogenized, adding 100 mL of seawater into a sterile blender for 1 min. The product was centrifuged for 10 min at 4000 g and ∼ 50 mL of supernatant was carefully collected, avoiding the movement or inclusion of solid debris. At this stage, a viscous supernatant was obtained due to the presence of elevated amounts of suspended solids, in addition to microorganisms and viral particles. Bacterial counts were conducted during this stage. Two mL of supernatant was sequentially filtered through nitrocellulose membranes of 5 μm, 0.45 μm, and 0.22 μm pore size (Millipore) to eliminate major particles. 100 μL of chloroform was added to 1 mL of the filtrate to remove the remaining bacterial remnants. After 30 s of vortex shaking, the tubes were centrifuged for 5 min at 10,000 g. Finally, 500 μL of the aqueous phase corresponding to the virion suspension was recovered, carefully avoiding the uptake of chloroform.

At least 30 clearly defined lysis plates were selected by gently picking them with sterile wooden sticks (toothpicks), and used to inoculate 1 mL of early exponential bacterial culture containing 10 mM MgCl2. They were incubated overnight at 20 °C and the isolation process was repeated at least three times to ensure the presence of a single lytic phage per tube. The phages obtained from the process were named according to the nomenclature norms proposed by Kropinski et al. [5], following the detail published in the REBASE database (http://rebase.neb.com/rebase/rebase.html). Presence of genes associated with a temperate life cycle (i.e. integration/excision genes) must be evaluated by molecular techniques (PCR-Sequencing) to finally ensure that our isolated is an obligately lytic bacteriophage [6].

steps.title: Bacterial cell counting (DAPI)
steps.instruction: Determine bacterial abundance in the sample by DAPI fluorescence microscopy following the detailed staining, filtration, mounting and counting procedure.

substeps.instruction: Stain the sample with DAPI (4′,6-diamidino-2-phenylindole‑dilactate, Merck).
Prepare three 10 mL serial dilutions of the stained suspension (1/10, 1/100, 1/1000) and add 4 % paraformaldehyde to each tube.
Filter each diluted suspension through a 0.22 µm polycarbonate membrane (Merck, Millipore) and let the filters dry on absorbent paper for 15 min.
Place 15 µL of a 2 mg L⁻¹ DAPI solution on a microscope slide, cover with the dried filter and incubate in a dark, damp box for 15 min at room temperature.
Remove the filter, wash it in 96 % ethanol for 10 s, then dry on absorbent paper for 1 h at 37 °C in the dark.
Mount the dry filter on a slide with 10 µL Vecta Shield mounting medium (Vector Labs) and cover with a clean cover glass.
Observe stained cells using a fluorescence microscope (excitation ≈359 nm, emission ≈461 nm) with a 100× objective and a 10 × 10 µm counting grid in the eyepiece.
Count at least 500 cells per sample; select the dilution that provides the required fields.
Calculate total cells per sample using the equation: (A × X × f) / (a × 1 mL) − 1, where A = filtration area, X = counted cells, f = dilution factor, a = area of the observed field.

steps.title: Phage isolation from mollusk tissue
steps.instruction: Extract and purify a virion suspension from collected mussel tissue.

substeps.instruction: Collect mussels, place in sterile containers and process the same day.
Excise 100 g of soft tissue, add 100 mL seawater and homogenize in a sterile blender for 1 min.
Centrifuge the homogenate for 10 min at 4 000 g and carefully collect ~50 mL supernatant, avoiding solid debris.
Filter 2 mL of the supernatant sequentially through 5 µm, 0.45 µm and 0.22 µm nitrocellulose membranes (Millipore).
Add 100 µL chloroform to 1 mL of the filtrate, vortex for 30 s, then centrifuge 5 min at 10 000 g.
Recover 500 µL of the aqueous (upper) phase, which contains the purified virion suspension.

steps.title: Optional phage enrichment
steps.instruction: Increase the number of specific phages before plaque assay, if desired.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL of the virion suspension to 20 mL of early‑exponential bacterial culture supplemented with 10 mM MgCl₂.
Incubate the mixture at 20 °C and monitor for medium clarification (indicating bacterial lysis), for up to 48 h.
After clarification, recover phages using the same chloroform‑filtration procedure described in the isolation step.

steps.title: Phage plaque assay (double layer)
steps.instruction: Quantify phage particles by the double‑layer agar technique.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mM MgCl₂ to TSB medium (culture medium) to supply required divalent cations.
Prepare lower‑layer agar: 1.5 % Bacto‑Agar (Difco) in TSB, autoclave and pour into Petri dishes.
Prepare upper‑layer agar: 0.7 % Bacto‑Agar in TSB, autoclave, keep at 45 °C in glass tubes (max 1 h) before use.
Grow the bacterial host to early exponential phase.
Make three serial dilutions of the enriched (or enriched‑optional) virion sample (1/10, 1/100, 1/1000).
For each dilution, mix 1 mL of diluted phage suspension with 0.1 mL bacterial culture and 3 mL molten 0.7 % agar (maintained at 45 °C).
Homogenize quickly and pour the mixture onto a plate that already contains the solid lower‑layer agar.
Allow the top agar to solidify, then incubate plates overnight at 20 °C.
Count clear lysis plaques and calculate plaque‑forming units (PFU) per millilitre for each dilution.

steps.title: Isolation of single lytic phages
steps.instruction: Obtain pure lytic phage isolates by repeated plaque picking and re‑infection.

substeps.instruction: Select at least 30 well‑defined lysis plaques using sterile wooden sticks (toothpicks).
Transfer each picked plaque into 1 mL of early‑exponential bacterial culture containing 10 mM MgCl₂.
Incubate the inoculated cultures overnight at 20 °C.
Repeat the plaque‑picking and re‑infection cycle at least three times to ensure isolation of a single lytic phage per tube.
Assign names to the isolated phages according to Kropinski et al. nomenclature and verify obligate lytic nature by PCR‑sequencing for temperate‑associated genes (optional).
